questions.stem: If a cache hit occurs 90% of the time and the cache access time is 2 ns, while main memory access time is 20 ns, what is the average memory access time? Provide your answer in nanoseconds.
questions.explanation: The average memory access time is calculated as: $0.9 \times 2 + 0.1 \times 20 = 1.8 + 2 = 3.8 \text{ ns}$.

questions.stem: Explain how spatial locality can improve the performance of a program that processes an array sequentially.
markingGuide: Describe how accessing consecutive memory locations benefits from spatial locality.
Explain how caches exploit spatial locality to improve performance.
questions.explanation: Spatial locality refers to accessing memory locations close to each other. When a program processes an array sequentially, it accesses consecutive memory locations. Caches can load entire blocks of memory, so accessing one element brings nearby elements into the cache, reducing future access times.

questions.stem: A system has a cache hit rate of 95% and a cache access time of 1 ns. If the main memory access time is 50 ns, what is the average memory access time in nanoseconds?
questions.explanation: The average memory access time is calculated as: $0.95 \times 1 + 0.05 \times 50 = 0.95 + 2.5 = 3.45 \text{ ns}$.

markingGuide: Discuss the speed difference between SRAM and DRAM.
